?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:181523
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Cancellation Application No. - 387 of 2021

Applicant :- Govind Prasad
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Bholeshwar

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Afshan Shafaut
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.  On 11.11.2021, notice was issued to opposite party no.2 through C.J.M. concerned.
2. As per the office report dated 11.01.2022, notice has been served upon opposite party no.2 through his heir.

3. Despite effective service of notice, none put his appearance on behalf of the opposite party no.2.
4.

Heard Shri Bholeshwar, learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Santosh Nigam, learned A.G.A. for the State-respondent and Ms. Afshan Shafaut, learned counsel for the High Court Legal Service Committee.

5. The instant bail cancellation application has been filed seeking cancellation of the bail granting order of opposite party no.2 dated 15.09.2021 passed by Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge Govind Prasad vs State Of U.P. And Another on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124325454/
1 POCSO Act in Case Crime No.0149 of 2021, under Sections 363,366, 376 IPC & Sections 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Jahanabad, District Fatehpur, during pendency of the trial in the court below.
6.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge Govind Prasad vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is the informant of the case and he has filed the instant bail cancellation application with a prayer to cancel the bail granted to opposite party no.2 on the ground that in spite of the fact that daughter of the applicant was well below eighteen years of age court concerned granted bail to opposite party no.2 and further after release on bail, opposite party no.2 continuously harassed the applicant to compromise the matter and in this regard, an FIR was also lodged by the applicant against the opposite party no.2 and others and the FIR lodged by the applicant has been annexed as Annexure No.5 to the affidavit.
7. Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case stated above, bail granted to opposite party no.2 be cancelled.

8. Per contra; learned A.G.A. for the State-respondent and learned counsel for the High Court Legal Service Committee opposed the prayer for cancellation of bail and submitted that after considering the entire facts of the case, court concerned granted bail to opposite party no.2 with a very detailed and reasoned order and if on the basis of the FIR of threatening, this Court starts cancelling bail granted to accused persons, then this Court will open pandora box and endless litigation will start between the accused and the victim and therefore, the instant bail cancellation application is devoid of merit and is liable to be dismissed.
9.
I have heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. The instant bail cancellation application has been moved by the applicant, who is informant of the case on the ground that after release on bail, opposite party no.2 pressurizes him for compromise and in this regard, an FIR was also lodged by the applicant against the opposite party no.2 and others.

Further as prosecutrix was below eighteen years of age, therefore, court concerned wrongly granted bail to opposite party no.2.
11.

From the perusal of bail granting order passed by the court concerned, which has been annexed with the instant bail cancellation application, it appears that with the reasoned order, bail was granted to the opposite party no.2 and while granting bail, court concerned considered every aspect of the case and therefore, I find no illegality in bail granting order dated 15.09.2021 passed by the court concerned.
12.

Further although from the Annexure No.5, which has been annexed alongwith the instant bail cancellation application, it appears that an FIR was lodged by the applicant in the month of September, 2021 against the opposite party no.2 and others to the effect that after release on bail,
opposite party no.2 is pressurizing the applicant for compromise, but I find force in the argument advanced by learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the High Court Legal Service Committee that if on such grounds, this Court starts entertaining the bail cancellation application, then this Court will open pandora box.

Govind Prasad vs State Of U.P. And Another on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124325454/
2 13.

sentences.text:
Further, the allegation of threatening and pressurizing was of September, 2021 i.e. of two years before and since then more than two years have been passed but there is no evidence on record,
which can show that in between two years, opposite party no.2 again tried to create pressure or threaten the applicant to compromise the matter, therefore, in my considered view, on stale ground of threatening, the bail granted to opposite party no.2 should not be cancelled.
14.

Further, law is settled that it is easy to reject a bail application but it is very difficult to cancel a bail already granted and for cancellation of bail, very cogent and overwhelming reasons must be available on record, which in my considered view is missing in the present matter.
15.
Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view, the instant bail cancellation application is devoid of merit and is accordingly dismissed.
Order Date :- 19.9.2023 Zafar  Govind Prasad vs State Of U.P. And Another on 19 September, 2023
